subject: Medimaps: processing locations, subprocessors, and cross-border transfer controls
messages:
From: Oliver Chen <oliver.chen@medimaps.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
Cc: security@medimaps.com
Date: 2028-07-19T14:12:00+02:00
Subject: Quick Q on where requests are executed (processing footprint)

Hi Evelyn,

Thanks for running through the initial overview earlier. Before we take this to Procurement I need a concise mapping we can share with our security reviewers:
- Which physical regions do inference requests hit for the hosted Redwood API when the account is configured for EU-only?
- Do any Redwood subprocessors (e.g., cloud providers, cache vendors, monitoring) ever receive plaintext request payloads outside the EU?
- If you have a high-level diagram or CSV inventory of subprocessors and their locations that would be great.

Also, what is the default retention for request-level artifacts (prefix/KV cache, short-term logs) and the deletion SLA? We're particularly sensitive to PII and would like the retention numbers to present to our DPO.

Appreciate a short written response we can include in our deck.

Best,
Oliver
Oliver Chen
Head of Security & Compliance
Medimaps
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
To: Oliver Chen <oliver.chen@medimaps.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-07-19T15:47:00+02:00
Subject: Re: Quick Q on where requests are executed (processing footprint)

Hi Oliver — thanks for the clear list. Below is a concise, shareable summary you can drop into your security review. I've attached a one-page processing map and our current subprocessor inventory CSV for your team. Happy to hop on a short call if you want to walk through it.

Key points (EU-only configuration):
1) Primary execution loci
   - By default, when an account is configured for EU-only execution, inference requests are routed to our EU fleet. Major compute regions in use today: eu-central-1 (Frankfurt), europe-west3 (Paris), and europe-west4 (Netherlands) depending on capacity and model variant.

2) Subprocessors and data exposure
   - Core compute: AWS (eu-central-1) and GCP (europe-west3) for primary execution. We do not send plaintext request payloads to third-party analytics vendors.
   - KV/prefix cache: hosted in-region using Redis-compatible managed clusters operated by our cloud provider within the same EU region. Cache entries are encrypted at rest and in transit.
   - Logging/monitoring: aggregated telemetry (latency, errors) is pseudonymized and sent to our observability backend; request payloads are not forwarded.
   - Backup/replication for Disaster Recovery (DR): we do offer cross-region DR replication but this must be explicitly enabled; by default no cross-region replication is configured for EU-only accounts.

3) Cross-border transfer controls
   - Legal framework: when cross-border movement is required (e.g., customer enables multi-region DR or in a rare forced-failover scenario), we rely on EU-approved Standard Contractual Clauses (SCCs) and additional contractual commitments.
   - Customer choices: you can (a) pin to EU-only, (b) allow EU-primary with optional DR to a secondary region, or (c) use our Dedicated/Private deployment options to keep all assets within a single VPC/region.

4) Retention and deletion
   - Ephemeral request artifacts (KV/prefix cache): default TTL is 1 hour; manual or programmatic purge available via the API.
   - Short-term request logs (for debugging): retained 30 days by default; can be shortened on request for enterprise contracts.
   - Audit traces / control-plane logs: retained 90 days and accessible via Console/Export; deletion of historical audit events follows regulatory retention needs and can be scoped per contract.
   - Deletion SLA: for ephemeral artifacts we can confirm immediate invalidation on purge. For backups/snapshots we guarantee secure deletion within 30 days of a deletion request unless otherwise specified in the contract.

Attachments: redwood-processing-map-2028-07.pdf (one-page map), subprocessor-inventory-2028-07.csv (full list + region column).

If it's helpful I can also include a short paragraph describing encryption at-rest (AES-256) and key management options (we support customer-managed keys for Dedicated and Private).

Best,
Evelyn Hart
Director, Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference

Thanks, Evelyn — this is exactly what we needed. A couple of quick clarifications for our DPO:
- You mentioned cache entries are encrypted at rest and in transit. Are the cache encryption keys managed by Redwood or can Medimaps provide a KMS key?
- If we enable DR replication later, will the replicated cache be stored in plaintext in the secondary region during the transfer window?

If easy to answer in a line or two that's perfect. Otherwise we can loop in procurement.

Oliver
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
To: Oliver Chen <oliver.chen@medimaps.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-07-20T09:04:00+02:00
Subject: Re: Quick Q on where requests are executed (processing footprint)

Hi Oliver — quick answers below, happy to expand in contract language if Procurement asks.

- KMS: for Hosted accounts keys are managed by Redwood by default. We offer customer-managed keys (CMKs) for Dedicated and Private deployments; for Hosted we can also support CMK wrap options under an enterprise addendum (we'll put this in the SOW).

- DR replication transfers: replication traffic is encrypted in transit (TLS) and the data remains encrypted at rest in the destination region. The data is not stored in plaintext during transfer — encryption keys are never transmitted in the clear. Replication is an opt-in feature; if you keep EU-only pinning and do not enable DR replication, no data leaves EU regions.

I'll loop Karthik and Marissa to flag procurement and to start drafting the narrow CMK language and the DR SLA clause if you want them in the next round.

Link for DPO: https://console.redwood.ai/docs/geo-processing#eu-data-controls

Best regards,
Evelyn
